notes: No code changed by this seat. Gaps for the owner, none needing code within scope: (1) The ContextVar that lets a run method build its app is inherited by tasks created while that run serves, so a tool handler inside an unlocked run could obtain an app; the lock was off at that start, so R29 is not touched, but it is a design-level leak of an app object. (2) A server started with the lock off keeps listening if the firm turns the lock on later; every tool call then refuses (tested), but the socket stays open until restart. Whether R29 means a running server must stop is a design question. (3) Calling the parent class unbound, MCPServer.sse_app(server), bypasses the subclass; that is deliberate circumvention outside the guarantee. (4) No remote alert exists, by design (Observability: local refusals only). The probe script lives in the session scratchpad, not in the repo or the run folder, so the runner did not run it; its claims are backed by the named pytest tests, which the runner does run.
